method: Fresh no-files Sol 6.1 max behavioral explanation, parent code inspection, then challenge and reconciliation before edits.
accepted_design: Scheme compiles and executes the complete input on every invocation; the original predicate checks the final result once after all repetitions.
Scheme frame indices are reclaimed only between complete evaluations; global bindings, macros, live values and compiled closure constants contribute roots.
Dynamic retains persistent primitive type graphs across iterations. Resetting outer bindings does not reconstruct those graphs.
Dynamic graph retention follows representative links and source definitions, including polymorphic captures behind nonrepresentative nodes.
Dynamic constructs the complete tagged output during each timed invocation; the extra complete dump after timing is another inference run over persistent state.
Stable slots and monotonically increasing construction identifiers have distinct purposes and must remain separate.
changes: Scheme test retains a captured mutable frame through a quoted closure in compiled code while unrelated evaluations create reusable frames.
Dynamic test retains a polymorphic capture after union with dynamic, reclaims an unrelated slot and verifies fresh construction identity on reuse.

validation.release_build: cargo build --offline --release --target wasm32-wasip1 --manifest-path benchmarks/wasm-reference/Cargo.toml --bin scheme --bin dynamic passed

exceptions_to_ten_line_target: Keep exhaustive source-form, primitive, type-constructor and tagged-output dispatch together. Mark/sweep transitions and lifetime regression tests expose complete invariants and are intentionally cohesive.
limits: This review covers these two reference ports, not the still-pending structural-port cohort.
No fresh performance observations were collected. Test-only edits produce byte-identical release Wasm to the previously validated complete canonical runs.
Scheme arbitrary cyclic mutable pair/vector collection remains outside the checked workload domain, as documented in PORTING.md.
Dynamic post-timer full-output audit is an extra invocation, not a retained snapshot of the last timed invocation.
decision: Accept both focused modules with the two lifetime regression tests. No runtime refactor is justified by this review.
